nodes.directText: This guide is meant to help document how rustc – the Rust compiler – works, as well as to help new contributors get involved in rustc development.
nodes.subtreeText: This guide is meant to help document how rustc – the Rust compiler – works, as well as to help new contributors get involved in rustc development.

nodes.directText: There are several parts to this guide:
nodes.subtreeText: There are several parts to this guide:

Building and debugging rustc : Contains information that should be useful no matter how you are contributing, about building, debugging, profiling, etc. Contributing to Rust : Contains information that should be useful no matter how you are contributing, about procedures for contribution, using git and GitHub, stabilizing features, etc. Bootstrapping : Describes how the Rust compiler builds itself using previous versions, including an introduction to the bootstrap process and debugging methods.

nodes.directText: Keep in mind that is a real production-quality product, being worked upon continuously by a sizeable set of contributors. As such, it has its fair share of codebase churn and technical debt. In addition, many of the ideas discussed througho
nodes.subtreeText: Keep in mind that rustc is a real production-quality product, being worked upon continuously by a sizeable set of contributors. As such, it has its fair share of codebase churn and technical debt. In addition, many of the ideas discussed throughout this guide are idealized designs that are not fully realized yet. All this makes keeping this guide completely up to date on everything very hard!

nodes.directText: The guide itself is of course open source as well, and the sources are hosted on . If you find any mistakes in the guide, please file an issue. Even better, open a PR with a correction!

nodes.directText: You can also use Rustdoc’s built-in search feature to find documentation on types and functions within the crates you’re looking at. You can also search by type signature! For example, searching for should find all functions that return a .
nodes.subtreeText: You can also use Rustdoc’s built-in search feature to find documentation on types and functions within the crates you’re looking at. You can also search by type signature! For example, searching for * -> vec should find all functions that return a Vec<T> . Hint: Find more tips and keyboard shortcuts by typing ? on any Rustdoc page!
